patterns.comment: the lexer only ever recognizes '//' -- skipWhitespace() has no block-comment branch, so /* */ is NOT a real CnR comment form. It's kept here purely as an editor convenience (so stray /* */ in a file at least renders as a comment instead of as broken syntax), not because the interpreter understands it.
patterns.name: comment.line.double-slash.cnr

patterns.comment: global preset variables, not lexer keywords -- pi/euler/phi/psi are BigFloat constants set at startup by the math bridge. true/false ARE real lexer keywords (TrueKw/FalseKw). null is not a TokType in this lexer at all; kept here defensively in case a later build adds it, but as written CnR has no null literal.
patterns.name: constant.language.cnr

patterns.comment: real control-flow/statement keywords in keywordTable(): var/print/if/else/while/for/function/return/try/catch/Throw, PLUS switch/case/default/break/continue and mutable, all of which genuinely exist as TokTypes and are parsed (parseSwitch/parseBreak/parseContinue). This language does NOT have do/import/using/namespace.
patterns.name: keyword.control.cnr

patterns.comment: switch/case/default/break/continue are real TokTypes (SwitchKw/CaseKw/DefaultKw/BreakKw/ContinueKw) parsed by parseSwitch()/parseBreak()/parseContinue() -- first matching case runs (no fallthrough), break exits a case or a while/for loop, continue is valid in while/for/switch.
patterns.name: keyword.control.switch.cnr

patterns.comment: only these have dedicated TokType entries (CharKw/StringKw/IntKw/LongKw/FloatKw/BigIntKw/BigFloatKw). bigDouble is a lexer alias for BigFloatKw, not a separate type. There is no bool/void/double keyword -- double-precision numbers are just the language's native 'var' number type.
patterns.name: storage.type.cnr

patterns.comment: (Type)expr casts -- the only ones the parser builds dedicated *CastExpr nodes for: (char), (char[]), (string), (Int), (long), (Float), (BigInt), (BigFloat) or (BigFloat(precision)). There is no (bool) or (double) cast. The inner (precision) in BigFloat(N) is left to #numbers/#operators to scope as an ordinary parenthesized number. BigFloat(N) ALSO has a standalone (non-cast) form -- see #functions -- used as `var x = BigFloat(50);` to build a zero-valued BigDecimal at N fractional digits.
patterns.name: storage.type.cast.cnr

patterns.comment: var[] is an array, var[][] a Matrix, var[][][]+ a Tensor -- all the same 'var' keyword with repeated brackets, not separate Matrix()/Tensor() constructors (those don't exist as callables)
patterns.name: storage.type.matrix.cnr

patterns.comment: Struct Name { ... } -- Name is the type being declared

complete builtin math-function whitelist from isMathBuiltinName() -- note arcsin/arccos/arctan (not asin/acos/atan), and ln alongside log/log10. These are distinct from the mathDefine()/symbolic MathLib bridge builtins below (#mathlib-functions), which operate on named symbolic functions rather than plain numeric args.
patterns.name: support.function.cnr

patterns.comment: BigFloat(N) standalone constructor form (not a cast) -- `var x = BigFloat(50);`. Highlighted as a callable alongside the type keyword above since it behaves like a builtin function in this position.
patterns.name: support.function.bigfloat-ctor.cnr

patterns.comment: mutex() constructs a fresh, independent OS mutex (shared_ptr<std::mutex>). It is an ordinary function call, not a type/cast -- 'mutex' the identifier is only meaningful when immediately followed by '('.
patterns.name: support.function.mutex-ctor.cnr

patterns.comment: native file I/O builtins -- readFile/fileExists throw a catchable runtime error on missing files; writeFile overwrites, appendFile creates-or-appends.
patterns.name: support.function.file-io.cnr

patterns.comment: MathLib bridge builtins, verified directly against callMathLibBuiltin() in math_bridge.inc: mathDefine (function definition, single- and multi-variable), mathEval, mathToString, mathDerivative, mathGradient (multivariable derivative -- distinct from mathDerivative), mathIntegral, mathDefiniteIntegral, mathTaylorSeries, mathDomain, mathDomainExact, mathImage, mathLimit, mathLimitAtInfinity, mathSum, mathProduct, mathIsBijective, mathInverse, mathNumericInverseAt, mathRoots/mathRootsImag, divisors. 'define' is a real short alias for mathDefine (name0=="define" is rewritten to "mathDefine" before dispatch) -- both forms genuinely work.
patterns.name: support.function.mathlib.cnr

patterns.comment: complexEval("expr string") -- the actual complex-number arithmetic entry point in math_bridge.inc. Parses and evaluates an expression string where 'i' is the imaginary unit and 'sen' is accepted as an alias for 'sin'; returns {re, im} (or a plain number if the imaginary part is negligible). This is genuinely how CnR does complex arithmetic -- there is no dedicated Complex type/literal in the core lexer (see #types), it's entirely string-expression-driven through this one builtin.
patterns.name: support.function.mathlib.complex.cnr

patterns.comment: MathLib bridge builtins for Matrix values (var[][] arrays), verified directly against callMathLibBuiltin() in math_bridge.inc.
patterns.name: support.function.matlib.cnr

patterns.comment: header/body ARE real lexer keywords (HeaderKw/BodyKw), unlike Server/start which are soft keywords.
patterns.name: keyword.control.http-options.cnr

patterns.comment: 'Server' and 'start' are soft keywords -- recognized by matching the identifier's text (peek().text=="Server"/"start"), not real TokTypes. Same treatment as the array/DB method names.
patterns.name: support.class.server.cnr

patterns.comment: request/response are ordinary scope-bound objects inside route handlers, not lexer keywords -- highlighted as known globals, not as language keywords
patterns.name: variable.language.cnr

patterns.comment: exact isDbMethodName() list: encode, push, find, delete, insert, save, load, count, findWhere, updateWhere, deleteWhere, findById, updateById, deleteById, orderBy, get, getById. Note 'push' is shared with the array-method list -- context (preceding Data/table identifier vs. array variable) disambiguates at runtime, but for highlighting purposes both patterns match the same way.
patterns.name: support.function.database-method.cnr

patterns.comment: Nodes NAME { StepA() { ... }; StepB(StepA) -> OnFail(Retry = N) { ... }; Fail(); } -- all four are real TokTypes (NodesKw/OnFailKw/RetryKw/FailKw).
patterns.name: keyword.control.nodes.cnr

patterns.comment: mutable is a real keyword modifier (MutableKw) used as `mutable var x = ...;` to get a cross-thread-visible cell. mutex itself is the TokType MutexKw but is used as a plain callable identifier -- see #functions for the mutex() constructor.
patterns.name: keyword.control.mutable.cnr

patterns.comment: .lock()/.unlock()/.tryLock() -- called on a mutex-valued expression (a mutex() literal, a mutable variable, or a struct field holding a mutex). Recognized by method-name text after '.', like the array/DB methods.
patterns.name: support.function.mutex-method.cnr

patterns.comment: the complete operator/punctuation set the lexer actually tokenizes. This DOES include ++/--/+=/-=/*=//= (PlusPlus/MinusMinus/PlusAssign/MinusAssign/StarAssign/SlashAssign are all real TokTypes, lexed and consumed by the parser for both plain variables and array elements) -- earlier documentation claiming these don't exist was wrong. There is still no %=, <<, >>, ::, or ?: in this lexer. '->' is kept only because Nodes blocks write `Step() -> OnFail(...)`, tokenized as separate '-' and '>' but read as an arrow.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.compound.cnr
